tooltip.tupenter.tick_scripts_enabled: Master switch. While ON, every script below runs ONCE PER TICK (20x/second) — like being a walking mcfunction file. WARNING: any script that sends a command or chat will absolutely flood the chat on a multiplayer server unless you guard it (#if) or the server has sendCommandFeedback off. Best used with conditional scripts that normally do nothing. /tupenter abort turns this off in an emergency.
tooltip.tupenter.tick_script_toggle: Arm or disarm this script FOR THE WORLD YOU ARE IN. Every world/server keeps its own on/off states — a script armed here stays off everywhere else.
tooltip.tupenter.tick_script_toggle_lock: Join a world to arm scripts — every world/server has its own on/off states, so there is nothing to toggle from the menu. Text edits still save.
tooltip.tupenter.delete_script: Delete this script (takes effect immediately). Deleting a Global script removes it from every world.
tooltip.tupenter.add_script: Adds a new Global script row (visible in every world, armed in none until you toggle it). WARNING: this reloads the screen — script text edits are kept, but unsaved changes in other tabs are discarded.
tooltip.tupenter.add_world_script: Adds a script that exists ONLY in the current world/server — other worlds never see it. Starts disarmed. WARNING: this reloads the screen — script text edits are kept, but unsaved changes in other tabs are discarded.
tooltip.tupenter.global_scripts: Script definitions shared across all worlds. The On/Off next to each one arms it for the CURRENT world only — keep nukeOnDeath here, arm it only where it is funny.
tooltip.tupenter.world_scripts: Scripts that belong to the current world/server only. Change worlds and this section shows a completely different list.
text.tupenter.scripts_no_world: Not in a world — arming toggles are locked (each world keeps its own). Global script text can still be edited.
text.tupenter.world_scripts_no_world: Join a world or server to see and edit its scripts.
tooltip.tupenter.chat_input_length: How many characters the chat bar accepts (vanilla: 256). What actually gets SENT still obeys the protocol — plain chat and /say-style commands cap at 256, other commands at 32766 — but Tupenter blocks over-limit sends with a local error instead of crashing your connection. Raise this to type long /customcommand definitions in chat, long client-side commands (no wire limit at all), or lines whose $...$ expressions evaluate to something short enough to send.
tooltip.tupenter.chat_selection: Click and drag over chat messages (with chat open) to select text, then Ctrl+C to copy it. Selections span multiple messages — soft-wrapped lines join with a space, message boundaries become newlines. Plain clicks still trigger chat links and click-events; only an actual drag selects.
tooltip.tupenter.ctrl_scroll_history: Hold Ctrl and scroll while the chat is open to step through your sent-message history in the chat bar (up = older, down = newer) instead of scrolling the chat log. Reuses vanilla's history navigation, so it saves what you were typing and restores it when you scroll back down to the bottom. Plain scroll still scrolls chat. On by default.
tooltip.tupenter.ctrl_space_send: Press Ctrl+Space in the chat bar to send the line, exactly like Enter — so you can do a manual send without moving your hand off the mouse. On by default.
tooltip.tupenter.auto_close_brackets: While typing a command or #directive line (and in the Mod Menu script editor), auto-pair ( [ { " and $: typing an opener inserts its closer with the caret between, selecting text then typing a bracket wraps it, typing a closer that's already ahead steps past it, and backspace inside an empty pair deletes both. $ only pairs where a $marker$ would actually evaluate (never in plain chat or inside a "quoted string"). Off by default.
tooltip.tupenter.lazy_execution: Evaluate each statement WHEN IT RUNS instead of all at once when you press Enter. This is what makes #wait useful: /attribute @s jump_strength base set 30 && #wait 2t && /tp @s $client.target_block$ reads the target block AFTER the attribute landed. Re-running the same line cancels its still-running previous instance (resend = restart, not stack); different lines run concurrently; /tupenter abort stops everything. Turn this OFF to restore evaluate-everything-at-Enter (an escape hatch — #wait then still delays, but with stale values).
tooltip.tupenter.chat_highlighting: Colors Tupenter syntax as you type: each && segment is styled by its statement form (commands get vanilla-style argument colors from a per-segment parse, #directives go gold with dimmed group parens, bare chat is yellow), $...$ markers are aqua, && separators gold. Also re-roots autocomplete so tab-completion works INSIDE later chain segments: /time set day && /weather cl<tab>. Commands containing $...$ markers no longer show as red errors.
text.tupenter.tick_master_off: §eThe master switch above is OFF — armed scripts (✔) stay armed but won't run until you flip it on. (/tupenter abort turns it off.)
tooltip.tupenter.tick_scripts:
One script per row — statement forms apply like custom command bodies: /command, #directive, bare text = chat. Every armed script runs once per tick, 20x/second.

§cThat matters on a server:§r anything leaving your client — a real /command or a bare chat line — is sent twenty times a second, which floods chat and can get you kicked. Guard those behind something usually false (#if, a key edge, #wait). §aTupenter's own work is different:§r #set/#local, conditions, /echo and /echohud stay on your client and send nothing, so a script built only from those is safe to run anywhere.

Arming is per world — a script armed here stays off everywhere else. Tick scripts never touch your resend history and never print #set notices; one with an error reports once and is skipped until you edit it. /tupenter abort stops everything.
option.tupenter.reset_on_new_session: Clear Resend History on New Session
tooltip.tupenter.reset_on_new_session: If enabled, your resend history is automatically cleared when you join a world or server.
tooltip.tupenter.rapid_resend_delay: How many ticks the key must be held before rapid-fire starts. Only applies in Press & Hold mode.
tooltip.tupenter.resend_filter: Controls which types of sent messages are recorded and replayed. Note: Changing this setting will clear your current history.
tooltip.tupenter.resend_mode: Press & Hold: Resend fires while the key is held down. Toggle: Resend fires continuously until the key is pressed again. Off: Disables the resend key.
tooltip.tupenter.message_delay: Ticks to wait between sending each individual message in a batch. Set to 0 for no delay.
tooltip.tupenter.suppress_feedback:
Controls whether command output messages are hidden in your chat while Tupenter is firing.
- Off: Never suppress.
- On: Always suppress while firing.
- Dynamic: Only suppress in Toggle mode, not in Press & Hold. Useful if you want feedback when testing (hold), but silence when running hands-free (toggled on).
Note: suppression is client-side only — the server still processes commands normally.
tooltip.tupenter.pause_tracking: If enabled, newly sent messages will NOT update the resend queue while Tupenter is toggled on. Useful to avoid accidentally changing what is being spammed.
tooltip.tupenter.history_depth: How many of your most recent messages Tupenter tracks as a batch. If above 1, Tupenter will remember the last X messages and resend all of them together each cycle.
tooltip.tupenter.resend_delay: Delay between each full batch of messages.
tooltip.tupenter.batch_mode:
Controls behavior when stopping mid-batch:
- Pause: Resume next time.
- Finish: Complete current batch.
- Interrupt: Stop and reset.
(Batches always complete if Message Delay is 0)
tooltip.tupenter.resend_amount: Tupenter will fire off X times in a single tick. Can cause lag or disconnects with higher values.
tooltip.tupenter.resend_order: Order in which history items in a batch are resent.
text.tupenter.preset_hint: §7One command per line — all fire together when you resend (with 'What to Resend' = Preset Messages). Blank lines are ignored. Note: unlike the Scripts tab, here a newline SEPARATES commands.
tooltip.tupenter.import_count: How many of your most-recent history entries 'Import from History' pulls in. Session history holds up to 50.
tooltip.tupenter.import_history: Fills the preset box with your current session history (one command per line), replacing what's in the box. Nothing is saved until you click Done.
tooltip.tupenter.permanent_messages: The list of messages or commands Tupenter will send when 'What to Resend' is set to Preset Messages.
tooltip.tupenter.enhanced_command_parsin: Master switch for ALL Tupenter scripting: && chains, math, variables (#set/#setdefault), loops (#repeat/#for/#foreach/#while), conditionals (#if), #wait, #silent, custom commands, and /calc. When disabled, Tupenter sends commands exactly as written.
tooltip.tupenter.max_commands_per_tick: How many commands Tupenter may send in a single game tick, across all running scripts. Larger scripts are automatically spread over multiple ticks. Raise this on your own server; lower it if a public server kicks you for spam.
tooltip.tupenter.max_commands_per_script: Upper bound on how many commands one EAGER line may expand into — rejected before anything is sent if it's over. Loops that send or #wait each iteration run lazily and are NOT bounded by this: a big #foreach / #while / #randomfill paces itself across ticks instead.
tooltip.tupenter.max_concurrent_scripts: How many scripts may be mid-execution at the same time. Mostly relevant when large scripts are spread across ticks. Use /tupenter abort to stop all running scripts.
tooltip.tupenter.command_chaining: Lets Tupenter split lines joined with && and send the pieces in order. Each segment picks its own form: /command, #directive, bare text = chat — so /say ready && weather clear says ready then CHATS the words weather clear. Tupenter still remembers and replays the original combined line as one history entry. Example: /weather clear && /time set day.
tooltip.tupenter.number_math: Evaluates $ ... $ expressions inside commands before sending. Supports math (+, -, *, /, decimals, parentheses, s for stacks x64), text in "quotes", comparisons (==, !=, <, >), conditions like $x > 5 ? "big" : "small"$, and functions: int(...), float(...), rand(min, max), pick(a | b | c) with expression options (quote literal text: pick("say hi" | "say nah")), sin/cos/tan (degrees), sqrt, abs. Write \$ for a literal dollar sign. Note: write 2*sin(x), not 2sin(x) — a bare s after a number is the stack suffix. A bad $...$ expression shows an error and sends nothing. Auto-detect additionally solves plain math like 32+4 or 3s outside NBT braces (never errors — unparseable text is sent as-is).
tooltip.tupenter.variables: Adds user variables. #set $name$ = value stores a value for the session (cleared on join if history reset is on); #local $name$ = value lasts only for that line and prints no notice. Use anywhere as $name$. Works mid-chain: #set $x$ = rand(1, 10) && /give @s stick $x$! Built-ins: $client.x$, $world.time$, ... plus any raw data via $client.nbt.<path>$ / $target.nbt.<path>$ (browse with /tupenter dump). See /tupenter vars.
tooltip.tupenter.loops: Adds loop directives. #repeat 5 (/say Tick $i$!) runs its (...) group 5 times with $i$ counting 1..5. #for $x$ in 1..10 step 2 (...) counts with full control. #foreach $mob$ in (zombie | skeleton | creeper) (/summon $mob$) runs once per item; ranges work too: #foreach $n$ in range(1, 10) (...). Groups nest and can contain && chains. Every loop is capped by Max Loop Iterations.
tooltip.tupenter.conditionals: Adds #if ($client.y$ > 60) (/say high) #else (/say low). The condition is any true/false expression; the (...) groups can hold full && chains and nested directives. For picking a value inside one command, use a ternary instead: /tp @s ~ ~$client.y > 60 ? 10 : 0$ ~.
tooltip.tupenter.max_loop_iterations: Runaway guard: the most iterations a loop may run WITHOUT sending a command or #wait before it's stopped. Loops that send or wait each iteration pace themselves across ticks and aren't capped, so big #foreach/#while/#repeat run as long as they need.
tooltip.tupenter.silent_directive: Hides command feedback on your own screen. Start a line with #silent to silence all of it, or wrap part of a chain: #repeat 5 (#silent (/give @s stick) && /say here!). Also suppresses #set notices. Works in chat, as a command, and inside custom command bodies. The server still processes commands normally — other players are unaffected. Related: #norecord at line start keeps a line out of the resend history; /echo shows text only to you.
tooltip.tupenter.aliases: Custom commands in the format signature = body, like a function definition: blink <distance:int=5> = /attribute ... — typed parameters sit with the name. Bodies can include commands, chat messages, && chains, $...$ expressions, directives (#repeat, #if, #silent, #wait, ...), or other custom commands. See /customcommand help for the type list, optional =default params, and examples. Reference params as $name$ or $1$..$n$. Edits here and via /customcommand both take effect immediately.
tooltip.tupenter.add_command: Adds a new command row. WARNING: this reloads the screen — command text edits are kept, but unsaved changes in other tabs are discarded.
tooltip.tupenter.delete_command: Delete this custom command (takes effect immediately).
tooltip.tupenter.wrap_toggle: Toggle a larger editor with word wrap and chat-style syntax colors (unmatched parens and unclosed $...$ glow red). Newlines format long entries — they're saved, survive collapsing, and still run as a single line. Enter auto-indents, Tab inserts spaces, and pasting multi-line text into the collapsed view auto-expands. Editing the collapsed single-line view replaces the formatted version.
